evidence: Committed static baseline: task/solution/solve.sh only copies the committed solution/app tree into /app (`cp -a "$(dirname "$0")/app/." /app/`) and deletes a stale DB at the DB_PATH under /app; it runs no generator, npm install, curl/wget or network fetch. package.json pins express 5.1.0 / better-sqlite3 12.4.1, which the agent image installs globally at those exact versions (environment/Dockerfile npm install -g express@5.1.0 better-sqlite3@12.4.1); the golden ships no node_modules and installs nothing. index.html loads only same-origin /styles.css and /js/*.js; styles.css has no @import/url(); no CDN or boot-time fetch. Seed: src/seed_data.json is byte-identical to environment/assets/seed_data.json (sha256 a1c65c80...7740 both) and is read from beside the module (db.js `path.join(__dirname,'seed_data.json')`). seedIfEmpty (db.js) seeds only when users is empty, inserts users/jobs/applications with their fixed seed ids, applications with constant created_at '2026-06-15T09:00:00Z', messages/notes in seed array order with seed-provided created_at, and read markers mapped deterministically via read_count to the autoincrement message ids, so every fresh run produces identical rows. No Math.random/randomUUID/Date.now in seeding. Wall-clock and randomness exist only for runtime-created rows: index.js:59 `now = () => new Date().toISOString()` and index.js:60 `uid = (p) => `${p}-${crypto.randomBytes(3)...}`` for new jobs/applications, plus session tokens (index.js:88). None of these is a pinned or graded value: the brief/notes state no fixed clock and no criterion grades a date, duration or generated id (grep of all judge.toml for clock/date/UTC/2026/time returned only timeouts and '15 seconds' liveness windows). Graded orderings use deterministic keys, not time or random ids: board columns by position (board.js:163, index.js:199), Activity 'newest first' by autoincrement id DESC (index.js:189), messages by autoincrement id (index.js:407-416), stale-move attribution by latest activity id (index.js:242). Random-id tie-breaks only affect ungraded orders (jobs with identical titles; conversation-list threads with no messages; candidate applications created within the same ms). Raw evidence (hash-verified against current frozen bytes) records 'seeded card order and internal notes are loaded' and 'restart keeps jobs, cards, order, messages and activity without reseeding' as passed:true, consistent with deterministic idempotent seeding.
